verdict: Capex cycle holds at ~$730B but HBM4 correction risk is materializing early — SK Hynix cutting HBM4 volumes 20-30%; MRVL-NVIDIA $2B partnership is the standout bull catalyst; CPO entering revenue phase.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM pricing (decelerating):** Q4-2026 conventional DRAM contract prices forecast +10-15% QoQ (vs Q1's +93-98% and Q2's +58-63%). Growth is sharply decelerating off a very high base. HBM3E contract pricing ~$13-17/GB, down from $17-20 peak in H1-2025. Memflation is moderating.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 ramp / correction risk (BEARISH flag):** SK Hynix cutting HBM4 volumes **20-30%** this year, dialing back conversion of HBM3E lines earmarked for HBM4 upgrade. Cited reason: NVIDIA Rubin platform components not fully optimized; more profitable to serve HBM3E + server DRAM demand. Samsung separately reported $1B+ in HBM4 sales. **This confirms the baseline correction-risk signal — SK Hynix is explicitly deprioritizing HBM4 ramp pace.**

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI capex (still accelerating, no guide-down):** Full-year 2026 total ~$730B: Amazon ~$220B, Google ~$195-205B, Microsoft ~$175B, Meta ~$130-145B. Microsoft Q3 capex +84% YoY; Amazon Q3 at $44.2B. No guide-down visible. AI capex aggregate is now exceeding operating cash flow at several hyperscalers.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400/Helios + custom ASIC:** AMD confirmed Helios specs: 3 AI exaflops FP4, 72 MI455X GPUs, 31 TB HBM4, ~1.7 PB/s bandwidth per rack. Google reportedly tapping AMD to co-design next-gen TPU hybrid ASIC (integrating on-package CPU for reinforcement learning). Custom ASIC CAGR tracking at +44.6%.

**Signal 5 — Optical/photonics (CPO entering revenue):** NVIDIA's first CPO Ethernet switch is in full production with shipments starting this fall. Coherent first CPO revenue expected in **December quarter**. Coherent InP capacity on track to double by end of 2026 — one quarter ahead of plan. InP still on allocation; demand 2x supply.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** Section 232 tariffs (Trump Aug 6) take effect **Dec 4, 2026** — minimum import price $0.38/W for modules, $0.22/W for cells, +15% tariff. FSLR facing pricing pressure from US panel inventory glut + tariff cost on imported inputs. No fresh catalyst for ENPH/NXT/ARRY in the last 24-72h.

**Signal 7 — Watchlist name catalysts:** See below.

| MRVL | +8% (prior period) | NVIDIA $2B direct investment + strategic partnership (NVLink Fusion; custom XPUs + scale-up networking); **Analyst Day Oct 6** — mgmt flagged expanded Google relationship |
| HIVE | N/A price | $350M 5-yr GPU cloud deal (2nd in 2 months); BUZZ HPC annualized ARR now ~$180M (~$145M contracted to come online Q4-2026) |
| AVGO | Soft | Recent soft AI guidance triggered sector sell-off; AVGO ~$345 range |
| MU/ALAB | 52-wk highs (recent) | Hot chip rally; BofA raised AI data center SAM to $2.2T |

No notable single-day ~5%+ moves with fresh catalysts on Oct 2 specifically.

---

## Context vs. Baseline

The baseline flagged HBM prices 'could enter correction after 2026' — SK Hynix's 20-30% HBM4 volume cut is an early confirmation of that risk. However, it does NOT mean demand is soft; it reflects Rubin platform timing slippage pushing demand pull to 2027. HBM3E remains tight. The MRVL-NVIDIA NVLink Fusion deal validates custom-ASIC/hyperscaler share-shift thesis while keeping MRVL inside the NVIDIA ecosystem.

---

## Signals Flashing

| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| DRAM pricing (Q4 QoQ) | Decelerating (+10-15% vs prior +58-93%) | Neutral/mild bear vs hot baseline |
| HBM4 ramp pace | SK Hynix -20-30% cut | BEAR — correction risk materializing |
| Hyperscaler capex | Still accelerating ($730B, no guide-down) | BULL |
| Custom ASIC (AMD/MRVL) | Gaining — Google+AMD TPU hybrid, MRVL-NVDA deal | BULL |
| CPO optical | Revenue-phase entry (COHR Dec Q) | BULL (but early) |
| Solar / policy | Section 232 effective Dec 4 | BEAR FSLR near-term; long-run domestic manufacturing tailwind |

---

## Most Important Development

**SK Hynix cutting HBM4 volumes 20-30% (Rubin delays).** This is the first concrete production-level confirmation of the baseline correction-risk signal. It does not mean the AI memory cycle is over — HBM3E stays tight and conventional DRAM prices are still rising — but it shifts the HBM4 demand/supply intersection toward 2027 and adds price-pressure risk in that generation sooner than the baseline assumed. Watch Q4 pricing prints and Rubin tape-out confirmation closely.
